packageRules.description: Renovate capitalises the lock-file maintenance subject, which the PR-title check rejects; keep it lowercase like every other title
Hold every update for 7 days so a malicious or yanked release is caught before it lands
A digest update carries no release timestamp, so under the default timestamp-required its stability-days status would stay pending forever; the hold still applies where the registry gives a timestamp
Group minor updates for review (prod scope by default)
Auto-merge dev-scope minor updates after cooldown

Pin dev-group tooling so the lockfile cannot outrun the cooldown. minimumReleaseAge governs when Renovate opens a PR, not what the resolver picks: with the global rangeStrategy:bump and an open-ended floor, `uv lock` resolves the newest release regardless. Observed 2026-07-25 on PR #901 — a patch update intended for ruff 0.15.22 locked 0.16.0, a minor, and Renovate reported 'a pending version that has not yet passed the Minimum Release Age threshold'. The 7-day supply-chain wait above was being bypassed silently on every dependency PR. Pinning is correct here and ONLY here: dev-group tools never reach the published wheel metadata. Do not copy this to a runtime dependency of a published library — an `==` pin there propagates into every consumer's resolve (see the shared MCP foundation repo #684/#692, where pinning pydantic broke the whole stack).
Auto-merge GitHub Actions digest updates after cooldown
Pin GitHub Actions to SHA for security
Pin PSR to v10 — block Renovate downgrades

requires-python is the supported-interpreter floor set by the Python support matrix (3.11 and up), not a runtime pin. The python rule above matches it too, and with rangeStrategy bump Renovate raised the floor to the newest 3.13 patch, dropping 3.11 and 3.12 from the published metadata. Placed after that rule so it wins.

The networkx line marked python_version < '3.12' stays on the 3.6 series: networkx 3.7 requires Python 3.12, so bumping this floor to 3.7 leaves Python 3.11 without an installable networkx. The python_version >= '3.12' line keeps getting updates.
Disable runtime version updates from mise (pinned in CLAUDE.md)

n24q02m-hull and fastretrieval are released by this stack and consumed right after release. pyproject.toml exempts them from uv's exclude-newer; this rule, last so no later rule re-applies a hold, keeps Renovate from holding them either, so the version Renovate proposes is the one uv locks.
